RESOLVED the 'Sports Coaching' Telangana-parity gap left open since 2026-10-09/10. A CAG Audit Report (No. 4 of 2018, Chapter 3, General & Social Sector, Government of Telangana - official source, cag.gov.in) confirms Telangana adopted the (combined-state) Andhra Pradesh Sports Authorities Act, 1988 via a Telangana G.O. in January 2016 to constitute the Sports Authority of Telangana State (SATS) as its own principal sports-policy body under the Youth Advancement, Tourism & Culture (Sports) Department - the same bifurcation pattern already documented for the Telangana Pharmacy Council, Para Medical Board and Nurses/Midwives Council. This is a genuine state-specific institutional fork (distinct from both the AP body and the national Sports Authority of India), so added 1 new Telangana career row: 'Sports Coaching - Telangana (Sports Authority of Telangana State - SATS)' (checkpoint 1, see upserts). Current-cycle (2026) departmental coach-recruitment vacancy specifics could not be confirmed and are flagged unverified in the row. The Physiotherapy gap remains open despite more searching tonight. Found that the Telangana State Para Medical Board (TGPMB, under the Telangana Para Medical Board Act 38 of 2006, adapted post-bifurcation from the combined-state A.P. Para Medical Board Act 2006) handles diploma-level paramedical courses/certifications (e.g. DMLT) and that Bachelor of Physiotherapy (BPT) degree ADMISSIONS are run separately via KNRUHS (Kaloji Narayana Rao University of Health Sciences, Warangal) counselling - but this only establishes who runs admissions, not who licenses/registers a physiotherapist to practice after graduation, which is the actual open question (mirroring Andhra Pradesh's dedicated 2019 Physiotherapy Practice Act). Could not confirm whether TGPMB, KNRUHS, or no body at all handles post-graduation physiotherapist registration in Telangana, so deliberately did NOT add a row rather than guess. The Telangana Para Medical Board Act 2006 definitions section (Section 2), which would list exactly which professions TGPMB registers, still could not be retrieved (WebFetch to indiacode.nic.in blocked by the same egress issue noted under Phase 3). Continued scanning the full careers list tonight (checkpoint 2) for remaining one-sided AP-vs-Telangana rows per the 2026-10-10 NEXT note. JUDGMENT CALLS (no Telangana-specific row needed, confirmed tonight): Speech-Language Pathology & Audiology (BASLP) and Occupational Therapy (BOT/BOTh) - both fall under the Rehabilitation Council of India (RCI), a central statutory body under the Rehabilitation Council of India Act, 1992; Section 13 of that Act requires enrolment on the single, national Central Rehabilitation Register to practise 'anywhere in India', confirmed via rehabcouncil.nic.in's official categories list (Audiologist and Speech Therapists is an explicit registrable category) - same national-body pattern as CA/CS/Architecture, no state fork exists. NEW OPEN ITEM surfaced tonight: Yoga & Naturopathy (BNYS) looked like a promising candidate for a genuine AP-vs-Telangana fork (by analogy to the Pharmacy/Nursing/Para-Medical/Sports-Authority bifurcation pattern), but the actual legal picture turned out to be murky even on the Andhra Pradesh side: found only the Andhra Pradesh Yogadhyayana Parishad Act, 1987 (an education/training body, not a practitioner-registration council), a Rajya Sabha reference to a 2014 AP government committee that recommended registration/accreditation legislation for Naturopathy practitioners with no confirmation it was ever enacted, and 2026 news of AP making registration compulsory for AYUSH CLINICS (not individual practitioners) via amendments to the AP Private Medical Care Establishment Act, 2022. Given a 2025 Rajya Sabha answer confirms there is no central law and registration is a state subject handled by 'respective State Indian Medicine Board' where one exists, there may be a genuine fork, but it cannot be stated confidently for either state without first nailing down what (if anything) AP's own existing 'Yoga & Naturopathy (BNYS)' row currently cites as its registering body - deliberately left untouched rather than guess.
